The story is a nuanced, original piece of character-driven fiction that avoids clichés. Rather than relying on overused expressions or predictable plot tropes, the author uses fresh, specific imagery—such as the vibration of the diesel engine settling into Ilse's back "like an old acquaintance who no longer says hello," or a wave disappearing "as if the river had considered something and discarded it." Even when touching on familiar rural themes (a stoic northern German character, an out-of-place city traveler with no cell service, a strained relationship with a child who moved to the big city), the story treats them with restraint, realistic dialogue, and subtle emotional depth, ending on an ambiguous and resonant note rather than a predictable resolution.
